articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document is the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), titled "SJAA EPHEMERIS." It is Volume 4, Number 2, published in February 1993.

articles.title: The Eye Piece
articles.summary: The article apologizes for a missed speaker at the January general meeting and provides an update on the Grant Ranch observatory project, which has been put on hold due to local opposition, prompting the board to explore alternative sites. It also outlines a comprehensive schedule of upcoming events, including star parties, general meetings featuring talks on Gamma Ray Bursters and SETI, and astronomy classes, alongside brief mentions of an ET asterism observation and a Lensless Wright Camera project.

articles.title: Dr. Jack Marling Talk
articles.summary: Dr. Jack Marling delivered a talk at a general meeting about astronomical filters and photographic equipment, focusing on Lumicon's specialized bandpass filters. He detailed filters like Deep Sky, UHC, O-III, and H-Beta, explaining their specific applications for observing different celestial objects and their utility beyond just light pollution reduction. The talk also covered gas-hypersensitization of photographic film and Lumicon's quality control processes.

articles.title: December at Fremont Peak by Paul Barton
articles.summary: Paul Barton recounts three December 1992 observing sessions at Fremont Peak, detailing varied weather conditions from clear and cold to foggy and windy. He describes the diverse astronomical equipment used by fellow enthusiasts, including new telescopes and astrophotography gear, and observations of celestial objects like Venus, the Orion Nebula, and M-27. Barton also shares personal anecdotes, such as encountering black ice, meeting a pregnant couple, and enduring long nights under the stars with fellow amateur astronomers.

articles.title: Double, Triple, and Multiple Stars
articles.summary: Patrick M. Donnelly's article outlines the critical factors for observing double and multiple stars, prioritizing sky conditions like 'seeing' and darkness as most important. It also details how properties of the star system itself, such as component separation and magnitude differences, affect observability. Finally, telescope characteristics like aperture and magnification are discussed, though their impact is often secondary to sky quality.

articles.title: Fremont Peak Continued -
articles.summary: The article recounts a successful outing to Fremont Peak, followed by a review of useful equipment for star parties: a durable vacuum coffee mug and a convertible Zelco light adaptable with an LED for stargazing. It also announces the 1993 San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) Board elections and a SETI speaker for the February 6th General Meeting, concluding with a comprehensive calendar of SJAA events for the entire year.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Status
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) provides an update on its telescope loaner program, detailing the current status of various telescopes. The list includes different types of telescopes, their current borrowers, and due dates, or indicates if they are available for loan. Members interested in borrowing equipment are instructed to contact Paul Barton to be added to a waiting list.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: This section, "ASTRO ADS," serves as a free classifieds service for noncommercial advertisers to sell astronomically related products and services. It features listings for various used astronomical equipment, including different types of telescopes (Newtonian, Classic C-8, Celestron 14, Takahashi refractor), binoculars, and associated accessories. Advertisements are submitted to an editor for a run of approximately three months.

articles.title: Lunar/Phases Date Rise Tran Set
articles.summary: This document presents a concise lunar calendar, detailing the dates and times for upcoming lunar phases including Full Moon, Last Quarter, New Moon, and an incomplete entry for First Quarter. For each listed phase, it provides the exact time, date, and the corresponding approximate rise, transit, and set times for the moon.

articles.title: Nearer Planets
articles.summary: This document provides astronomical data for several planets—Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn—and the Sun (SOL) across three dates in February. For each celestial body, it lists its distance in Astronomical Units (AU), apparent magnitude, and a series of four numbers which likely represent observation times such as rise, transit, and set times for the specified dates. The Sun's entry also includes its stellar classification (G2V), absolute magnitude, and equatorial coordinates (RA and Dec).

articles.title: Astronomical Twilight
articles.summary: This document, titled 'Astronomical Twilight', provides a tabular listing of the start and end times for astronomical twilight across several dates in February, identified by both Julian Dates and conventional dates. This information is essential for astronomers to determine when the sky is dark enough for deep-sky observations, aiding in observation planning and scheduling.

articles.title: Siderial Time
articles.summary: The document provides specific sidereal time values for various astronomical events, including Transit Right, Ascension, and Local Midnight, corresponding to particular dates in February, all at 0000 PST.

articles.title: Darkest
articles.summary: This document lists specific astronomical times for "Darkest Saturday Night, Feb. 20," noting sunset, twilight end, and moonset. All times and dates are provided in Pacific Standard Time, indicating optimal dark sky conditions for observation.

articles.title: Offices and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the individuals serving in various offices and on the Board of Directors, including their titles such as President, Vice President, Treasurer, Secretary, and Directors. Each entry is accompanied by a contact phone number. It serves as a directory for the organization's leadership.

articles.title: Ephemeris Contributors
articles.summary: This document lists contact information, including names and phone numbers, for individuals designated as 'Ephemeris Contributors' and one 'Editor'. It serves as a directory for these specific roles.

articles.title: Comet Comments
articles.summary: This article reviews comet activity during 1992, highlighting new discoveries by both amateur and professional astronomers and the recovery of several returning comets. Key updates include the successful observation of Periodic Comet Swift-Tuttle, which debunked initial fears of an Earth collision in 2126, and the discovery of the distant object 1992 QB (1), whose classification remains uncertain. The piece also notes the reclassification of Periodic Comet Wilson-Harrington as a comet and provides brief updates on Periodic Comet Kojima and Periodic Comet Ohshita, with the latter expected to produce a meteor shower.

articles.title: PERIODIC COMET SCHAMASSE (1992x)
articles.summary: This document provides an ephemeris for Periodic Comet Schamasse (1992x) detailing its celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination), elongation, and estimated visual magnitude from late January to mid-March 1993. The data is presented in a tabular format to assist observers in locating the comet.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP
articles.summary: This document is a membership application form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), outlining different membership tiers and their costs, including options for individual membership and a bundled subscription to Sky & Telescope. It provides instructions on how to apply or renew, including contact details for the treasurer and general association information. The document also mentions the SJAA's monthly publication, "EPHEMERIS," and a 24-hour information hotline.
